@Don Sizemore, @Akio Sone, @William Hahn, @John D. Martin III, and the rest of the UNC team has given the go-ahead on merging the full https://github.com/gdcc/dataverse-jsf-tests repository into upstream.

UNC will be moving into a lower-overhead model depending heavily on upstream validation here on out.

The proposed model is a phased deployment. gdcc/dataverse-jsf-tests and uncch-rdmc/dataverse-jsf-tests will be immediately put into read-only mode. The tests will be merged into upstream, and the repositories will remain as such for a few months or so, while we at UNC figure out how we can pull upstream tests for our own use cases. Thank you!

@Philip Durbin 🚀
Sounds great! You'll be making a PR?
There's some technical debt that I want to address first, but yes I'll be making the PR!
do you have a timeline on when upstream wants it merged?
yesterday :smile:

tests/dataverse-jsf-tests ? or tests/playwright ?

Hmm, tests/jsf?

Shorter, sweeter. :smile:
SGTM
@Oliver Bertuch unless you want them under src/test somewhere?
https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/issues/12797
https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/pull/12798
This ports the repository as is

for sure
awesome, thanks
and thanks for the PR!
You have @Don Sizemore to thank. He was one of the strongest advocates from the very beginning
it's like a shiny new toy

It will continue to point at the old repo for a while
Until I address the technical debt and remove the UNC references
so this is more of a dump, a snapshot

not a living thing
dead code
doesn't execute

For now

But if it is used in its current state and y'all start adding tests
it will be unusable in a few weeks

Give me a few weeks (two or three) and I will make it fully extensible and usable for everyone
Sure, please take your time. Should I assign the PR to you? And put it in "in progress" on the board? Is that the right state?
Yep. I can also make it a draft PR if that helps

Philip Durbin 🚀 said:

Hmm, can you at least add a note at the top of tests/jsf/README.md? TODO: Clean up these docs, blah blah or something?

Added these to the top

Thanks and thanks for making it draft. I added it to "in progress" and assigned it to you.

For me, part of the definition of done is that the code not be dead. It should be executed by CI.
Mostly I'm just glad we're getting the tests upstream! :tada:
This PR has to be merged before the workflows can repoint to it anyways
we could take them live immediately after the merge
Huh. I imagined it would be one PR.
That would cause conflicts in this: https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/pull/12783
I'm trying to go as slow as possible so that nobody's workflow is disrupted and tests remain green throughout

By phased deployment my general idea was:
Phase 1: Get a dead dump/snapshot into upstream
Phase 2: Wait for 12783 to pass review
Phase 3: Clean up UNC references, technical debt within upstream
Phase 4: Activate the tests/jsf folder
Phase 5: Re-jig this pipeline for UNC's use
I think I missed the part about phased development.
I would advocate for this as it keeps disruption to a very minimum
#12783 has merge conflicts. I put it in "ready for triage" earlier today. Is that the right status?
It's in the making releases.rst file, I might git rm it tomorrow?
thank you so much for working with me on this!
sure!
I was thinking you'd merge the latest from develop but whatever works.
Yep, I did exactly that
great

I went ahead and closed the draft PR. I liked your idea more Phil, it's supposed to be one full PR where the code is both added and activated. In fact, this might actually be a really good excuse for me to try out: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/get-started/about-stacked-prs

My ETA is about 3 weeks
sounds fine, thanks!

Promise not to hate me. Here's a crazy thought. What if we'd create a Maven Submodule (as mentioned for API tests, too) and use a JUnit test to trigger running the Playwright tests? (Not asking to transform the tests from Node to Java here, just make them more accessible :wink: ) This might be a pipe dream around using https://github.com/eirslett/frontend-maven-plugin
I just left a lengthy review on #12783. Good job @Ash Manda! :heart: I do still have some more things for you... :grimacing: :see_no_evil:
It will take a long time to address some of those review comments
We cannot run JSF and API tests in parallel. Runners limits for free orgs is 20, we'd increase the number of parallel runners to 4. Dataverse frontend would suffer
Coveralls also doesn't support piecemeal XML reports. So we need to fold in your unit tests action into our workflow and generate a combined report.

There is a reason why I made the integration tests run three times, which is flaky tests. A lot of the time seeing an integration tests job fail, simply re-running it would get it to pass. If they run three times in parallel, say one passes and two fails, we know on the spot which test is flaky. That's a whole 40min re-run saved for developers. If all three fail, we know for sure that its not a flaky test

With GHCR uploads/downloads we are adding another point of failure into our workflow. GitHub artifact upload/download for our purposes here is "free". It costs 10 seconds up and down and it gives devs an easy download if they want to replicate the exact container setup.
Thank you for the detailed review! I'll share my thoughts there too
Anyone up for a campfire and a fireside chat in a cozy Zoom room to talk about this?

Raw notes from today's meeting. Very raw.

**Push to GHCR if secrets are available AFTER all the tests pass. Multi-arch image.
container_base_push.yml => we want to look Into ARM runners
We need to look into CodeQL parallelized runners running them sequentially
Phil, Oliver, Ash agree on unnecessary runners. Cut them down. Especially CodeQL
We want to decouple the API and JSF tests, before that CodeQL needs to go away. It is possibly replaced by SonarQube
**R1: Integration Tests

R2: Chrome -> R2: Firefox

-> R3: Webkit

All end at the same time
pom.xml <JaCoCo>
Take a JaCoCo report from each and merge them together:
-> Unit Tests
-> Integration Tests
-> API Tests
-> JSF Tests Chrome
-> JSF Tests Firefox

-> JSF Tests Webkit
maven_unit_test.yml does codecoverage
Code Coverage is out of scope for the current PR
Instead of mangling the JaCoCo agent, add a script to the base container to attach the JaCoCo agent.

Container base / modules /docker script / startinForeground.sh
compose.yml
Add more agents: Java Agents setting
Tell maven to fold the jacoco cli and agent images into the build file (maybe you don’t need the cli)
This is part of the scope for this PR
Maven Cache Management: Figure out NPM Caching
Playwright, Chromium, Firefox, and Webkit => Once they’re merged into upstream.
NPM Cache
Future Optimization: Figure out how to use the maven cache more to reduce per-branch maven. Then look into npm caches
mvn verify by default runs mvn package BUT BUT BUT there are skip flags present to skip the packaging steps.
@Ash Manda you're supposed to be on vacation!
That's what I said!! :smile:
I am always on vacation! This is fun!
I addressed almost all of the concerns we had in today's meeting except for caching. Which we can't do anyways because the JSF tests aren't in the main repo

The way I'm planning to handle it is that I am also rewriting the JSF tests repository from TypeScript into Java. By the time we're ready to bring it in, it should be able to fold directly into upstream
Ah, I was wondering about that. Backend devs would probably prefer Java anyway. :smile:
Tests pass successfully in Java: https://github.com/uncch-rdmc/dataverse/actions/runs/38826031860/job/116733594566?pr=108
Okay so i have a problem
I translated the entire suite into Java yes. But it still uses the microsoft playwright library
WOWzers! That must have been a lot of work!
This library is known for "strongly" preferring Ubuntu. I don't know if it'll break anything if its added to the project. Its known for not playing very well on Fedora/RHEL
The project is live at: https://github.com/gdcc/dataverse-jsf-tests/tree/java
If we put the tests into a submodule, most people probably will never get in touch with them. Maybe that's fine then?
I was wondering if someone can help me understand the blast radius of folding this into the upstream repo
Sure. What would you need?
going through the pom.xml and seeing if any libraries would cause problems for developers?
playwright is definitely one
The whole point of this exercise is to let developers run tests freely right
If that library is the only one, I might try switching to Playwright in Containers
I can take a look. But as I said, by making it a submodule, this is a part of upstream, but not mixed into the Dataverse source tree.
That makes it alot less risky
I thought we wanted to make it part of the source tree?
In any case, thank you so much!
I would advise against that. Please note that the two of us never talked about this here before, so my opinion might be different to what @Philip Durbin 🚀 said / wants / needs. :see_no_evil:
I just want the JSF tests in the main "dataverse" git repo so that tests are versioned alongside the code.
submodule ain't gonna do that right?
My advice would be to put the code under modules/dataverse-jsf and make it a submodule to the parent as well as using the parent in the module.
Ah, I think I know where the confusion comes from!
I'm talking about a _Maven_ submodule, not a _Git_ submodule!

Maybe just modules/jsf?

Or modules/jsf-tests?
Or under tests/jsf. I thought that was the original plan. :smile:
Again, I'd advice against that. Looking at a lot of other Java projects, if you have more tests for another module, they mostly use the module name and add a suffix
I still have to give developers a way to run these tests locally on RHEL
I'm not sure what we're talking about. Getting lost.

my bad.

Little bit of context

The playwright tests are now in Java. Which is good
But playwright doesn't work well on RHEL. Only on Ubuntu. The maven package
right, moving from JS/TS to Java was a big change
Most of our developers use RHEL afaik

Not for development. And I'm not most :sweat_smile:

Don't they? I thought RHEL was the recommended dev platform?
No, deployment platform
yes, RHEL for prod
IQSS AFAIK uses Macs exclusively, I'm on Fedora.
right
Not sure about the other core team members Vera and Eryk (not tagging them for now)
I _think_ Jim uses Mac as well?
I'd still feel better if someone more knowledgable used AI to see if any of these modules will cause an issue: https://github.com/gdcc/dataverse-jsf-tests/blob/java/pom.xml
Eryk is on Linux. Jim is on Windows. Not sure about Vera.
I don't see anything other than Playwright
/me checks out the code now
we probably want to run these tests on a deployment platform too
As long as the tests are not tied into the core code in any way (via Maven), they won't hurt anything in the core code.
Say a QA or Test server with an RC
We already have a couple little Maven projects in the core code that aren't tied in.
(I think @Oliver Bertuch has argued that they should be tied in.) :sweat_smile:
once again thank you so much for taking time to help me through this!
oh sure
Instead of <groupId>edu.harvard.iq</groupId> should we use org.dataverse? :thinking:
I agree we should use profiles per browser. The profile should keep the execution config, making the "skip" flags obsolete.

Either cd modules/dataverse-jsf; mvn verify ... or mvn -f modules/dataverse-jsf verify ...

If you have any reviews for that repo, they're always welcome! It's best to make changes right now
Ok, so a maven submodule. Tied in. Not a separate Maven project on the side that happens to be in the same git repo.

:point_down:

ha, maybe

sure, I have no problem

in Dataverse 10, I mean :smile:

yeah, get a topic, get a room! :smile:

yeah, I would use AI for that :smile:

if you would prefer structural changes, I'm more than happy to make them!

https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/.github/workflows/dataverse_jsf_tests.yml

But, its garbage that let us turn off Jenkins quickly!

https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/pull/12886

@Ash Manda any insights into why the individual JTs run sooooo slow? Is it just the CI runners not being beefy enough?
the JSF tests?

there's a 2.5 second delay between each action
Interesting! Is the UI that unreactive?

(I have zilch XP in this kind of testing)

No no no, I'm saying it's really bad we core devs never noticed this kind of problem!
It shouldn't be like that!
I'd say shitty dev job, but in fairness: manual testing probably was never at sub-second speed of clicking... :see_no_evil:
Wondering if PrimeFaces is the culprit here with all the AJAX stuff going on.

I've also not investigated WHY dataverse crashes when the robot goes fast. By parallelizing the suite, we already got a ton of time savings. We could reserve Webkit and Firefox testing only for the develop branch. That would get you back 35mins in time per PR.
It's much more efficient than any cuts we could make to the delay
Hmmm... Here's a somewhat different idea. What if we tie execution of them to a state?
Let's say once a PR enters "ready for review", we want them to run
ready for review is a board state right, not a PR tag?
It's also a data field on the PR

The chance something changed in the backend code that only affects Mozilla seems... Far fetched. If someone breaks a page, this will probably show in Chromium already. If someone changes JSF code, this will need to be tested with all the engines.
So maybe we can make the feedback loop in "early stages" of a PR faster than towards the end
I didn't quite get you
:see_no_evil:
Let me rephrase. A dev works on some Java code backing the JSF pages or even below that, in the EJBs/services.
If some of these changes break the JSF UI, it seems the chance it only breaks for one browser, but not the others is slim.
While on the other hand if someone works on JSF code (XHTML, CSS, JS, updating PrimeFaces ...), this might not break for all browsers.
Ohhh
Well, I've dealt with at least three PRs where everything worked on Firefox, but not Chrome or Webkit
That was one of the reasons why it even has three browsers in the first place
It was like playing whack-a-mole

in fact 4-5 tests in the suite are disabled in webkit because I couldn't figure out how to make them work on webkit, but they work just fine on Chrome and Firefox

Backend code, I've never touched JSF in the past year

I stand corrected. :see_no_evil: Well, then there's not really much we can do.

Overall, this is very cool. I'm trying to run a single test. This works:

LOGIN_ADAPTER=builtin DV_USERNAME=dataverseAdmin DV_PASSWORD=admin1 DV_FULL_NAME="Dataverse Admin" HEADED=true SLOW_MO=0 mvn -f modules/dataverse-jsf-tests verify -Ddataverse.test.jsf.browser=chromium -Dit.test=VersionHistoryJT

However, if I try to pare it down like this...

mvn -f modules/dataverse-jsf-tests verify -Ddataverse.test.jsf.browser=chromium -Dit.test=VersionHistoryJT

... I get this error:

VersionHistoryJT.testVersionHistory(Page, JsfFixtures)[1] » IllegalState Could not start chromium and log in

This version works, no errors:

LOGIN_ADAPTER=builtin DV_USERNAME=dataverseAdmin DV_PASSWORD=admin1 DV_FULL_NAME="Dataverse Admin" HEADED=true mvn -f modules/dataverse-jsf-tests verify -Ddataverse.test.jsf.browser=chromium -Dit.test=VersionHistoryJT
lemme look into it

LOGIN_ADAPTER=builtin DV_USERNAME=dataverseAdmin DV_PASSWORD=admin1 DV_FULL_NAME="Dataverse Admin" HEADED=true mvn -f modules/dataverse-jsf-tests verify -Ddataverse.test.jsf.browser=chromium -Dit.test=DatasetLifecycleJT

so the CI/CD on GitHub sets ENV variables

During the review I had the thought: what if we add default config to the POM, but then thought hey the vars are all set in CI. Forgot about local testing... Should we use the POM as the default source of thruth, still allowing overrides by prop or env?

I'd be happy with less to worry about in dev. :smile:
